clue.text: Meat pie looked unhealthy and pale

parts.note: a pasty is a pastry case filled with meat, a Cornish speciality
faced, as a house faced or looked south

explanation.surface: Someone ate a meat pie and then turned pale and sickly.
explanation.walkthrough: A PASTY is a British folded pastry pie, classically from Cornwall.
explanation.definitionFit: A compound adjective for a complexion drained of colour, the look of someone ill or indoors too long.

clue.text: Treated lung and time off demands foreign cash

indicators.note: treated in the sense of processed or worked on, so the letters of lung are rearranged

parts.note: off in the sense of odd or not right, which is rum in British slang

explanation.surface: A patient's lung treatment and time off work come with a bill in foreign money.
explanation.walkthrough: RUM here is the old British adjective for strange or peculiar, matching 'off'.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the currency of Bhutan, so it is money from abroad.

clue.text: See 23
Order big one to be inserted

indicators.note: to be inserted tells us the piece for one goes inside the piece for big

parts.note: big in the sense of fat or stout
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone orders a large item to be fitted into place.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiat is an authoritative decree or command, from the Latin for 'let it be done'.

clue.text: Procreate also after having left mother country's counterpart

indicators.note: after having places the word for also behind the letter for left

parts.note: to father is to beget or procreate
and is a synonym of also

explanation.surface: An instruction to have children and then leave home.
explanation.definitionFit: The motherland and the fatherland are both terms for one's native country, the masculine version being its counterpart.

clue.text: End of the line when stuffed on stage?

parts.note: stuffed after a big meal means full
a stage on a journey is a stop or halt

explanation.surface: An actor overeats and reaches the end of their lines on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'End of the line' looks like a railway terminus, but it is a line of text.
explanation.definitionFit: The punctuation point ending a sentence marks where a line of writing closes.

clue.text: Container has tons made by old Peruvian people

parts.note: the Incas ruled ancient Peru, so their adjective is Incan

explanation.surface: A vessel holding tons, built by the ancient people of Peru.
explanation.definitionFit: A metal can for food or drink is a common container.

clue.text: Unspecified number supporting earlier Greek festival

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits beneath, so the number comes last

parts.note: ago means in the past, earlier
N stands for an indefinite number in mathematics

explanation.surface: A number propping up some earlier event at a Greek celebration.
explanation.definitionFit: In ancient Greece this was a public contest or festival of games, athletics or music.

clue.text: Auckland's first great inn revitalised country

indicators.note: first means only the opening letter of the Auckland word is used
revitalised means given new life, so the letters of great inn are rearranged

explanation.surface: A traveller praises a refurbished hotel in New Zealand's largest city.
explanation.definitionFit: A South American nation, so simply an example of a country.

clue.text: Addiction evil and good after university

indicators.note: after places the evil and good pieces behind the university letter

parts.note: a sin is an evil act

explanation.surface: A student's drug habit, an evil that follows university.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a noun: 'using' is slang for habitual drug taking.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking drugs habitually is called using, so the gerund names the habit of addiction.

clue.text: Most High to examine everyone within

indicators.note: within puts the word for everyone inside the word for examine

parts.note: to test is to examine
all means everyone

explanation.surface: God, the Most High, examining everyone inwardly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Most High' looks like a title for God, but here it is just the superlative of high.
explanation.definitionFit: A superlative adjective meaning of the greatest height.

clue.text: Crazy Clio stuffs chicken — here it's said she dwells

indicators.note: stuffs means the scrambled name is packed inside the bird

parts.note: a hen is a female chicken

indicators.note: crazy signals that the letters of Clio are jumbled

explanation.surface: A mad muse is stuffing a chicken at her supposed home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it's said' means 'reputedly', not a sound signal: Clio is the Muse of history, and the Muses were said to live on this Greek mountain.
explanation.definitionFit: Mount Helicon in Boeotia was the legendary home of the Muses, Clio among them.

clue.text: Right hand closed around before all others

indicators.note: closed around tells us the hand piece wraps round the letter for right

parts.note: a fist is a closed hand

explanation.surface: A right hand clenched around something before anyone else grabs it.
explanation.definitionFit: Coming ahead of everything else in order is being at the front of the line.

clue.text: Neurotransmitter on stonier ground

indicators.note: ground as in crushed or milled, so the letters of on stonier are rearranged

explanation.surface: A brain chemical found on rockier terrain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ground' looks like a noun meaning terrain; it is the past tense of grind.
explanation.definitionFit: This chemical messenger carries signals between nerve cells and influences mood.

clue.text: Material witness right on the mark

parts.note: to see is to witness
a mark is a con man's target, a dupe or sucker

explanation.surface: A witness whose evidence is exactly accurate about the material facts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right on the mark' reads as one idiom meaning accurate; it splits into R and the mark, the victim of a con.
explanation.definitionFit: A light puckered cotton fabric, often striped, so a type of cloth.

clue.text: Seed-spiller up and back in very little time

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the biblical name is read from bottom to top

parts.note: in Genesis Onan spilled his seed on the ground
to back someone is to second or support them

explanation.surface: A sower working back and forth across a field in no time at all.
explanation.walkthrough: Onan is the Genesis figure who spilled his seed.
explanation.definitionFit: A billionth of a second, the standard example of a vanishingly brief interval.

clue.text: Offend down under when uncooked seafood arrives?

definitions.meaning: an Australian slang phrase for trying to deceive or take liberties with someone, giving offence
read literally, a crustacean in its unboiled state turning up

explanation.surface: Australians taking offence when the shellfish is served raw.
explanation.walkthrough: 'down under' means Australia, where this idiom is used.
explanation.definitionFit: Australian slang for trying to put one over on someone; literally, uncooked shellfish arriving.

clue.text: Agitated state ends with 'immobilise'

parts.note: tails are the rear ends of things
to pin is to hold fast so it cannot move

explanation.surface: An anxious state that ends in someone being frozen in place.
explanation.definitionFit: Figuratively, a state of panic or chaos, from an aircraft spiralling down out of control.

clue.text: One parking round about little man authorised

indicators.note: round means the word for one goes about the letter for about

parts.note: an ace is a one in cards
C, for circa, means about
P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking
Ted is a short form of Edward, a little man's name

explanation.surface: Someone parking around a small man has been given permission.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that has been approved or sanctioned has been officially allowed.

clue.text: Sacked — failed to entertain society girl

indicators.note: to entertain is to take in as a guest, so the society girl goes inside

parts.note: a machine or plan that died has failed
a miss is a girl

explanation.surface: An entertainer fired after failing to amuse a debutante.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entertain' suggests a show, but it means 'hold within'.
explanation.definitionFit: To be fired from a job is to be let go, as an employee shown the door.

clue.text: Sons stay awhile — such a beautiful night

parts.note: to tarry is to linger or stay awhile

explanation.surface: Children lingering outdoors on a lovely night.
explanation.definitionFit: A clear night sky full of stars is the classic beautiful night, as in Van Gogh's painting.

clue.text: This Latin-American cheat

parts.note: hoc is the Latin for this

explanation.surface: A con man from Latin America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Latin-American' reads as one word; split it into 'This Latin' and 'American'.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to trick or hoax, from the conjuror's patter phrase.

clue.text: Raft starts from here as taking folks up Limpopo

indicators.note: starts from means take the first letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: A river raft setting out from here, carrying people up the Limpopo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raft' looks like a boat, but a raft of things is a large number.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean a large quantity, as in a raft of ideas or a whole load of them.

clue.text: Excellent rescue dog detailed to enter clubs twice

indicators.note: to enter means the shortened dog goes inside the pair of club letters
twice gives the club letter two times over

parts.note: C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs

indicators.note: detailed means with its tail, the final letter, cut off

parts.note: Lassie is the famous collie of film and television who rescues people

explanation.surface: A first-rate rescue dog sent to join two golf clubs.
explanation.definitionFit: First-class or of the highest quality, as a timeless model of its kind.

clue.text: Guard hollow chamber

definitions.meaning: the Latin call 'beware', used by British schoolchildren keeping watch, so to keep guard

explanation.surface: A sentry keeping watch over an empty room.
explanation.walkthrough: As an interjection it was British public-school slang shouted by a lookout when a teacher approached.
explanation.definitionFit: A Latin warning to look out, and also a natural cavity in a hillside.

clue.text: Matter for discussion on Eastern Cape displaced

indicators.note: on means the discussion piece comes after the other two

parts.note: C is the map abbreviation for Cape
a topic is a subject to be discussed

explanation.surface: A debate about people displaced from South Africa's Eastern Cape province.
explanation.definitionFit: In medicine it describes something in an abnormal position, such as a pregnancy outside the womb.

clue.text: Beelzebub's presence unfortunate camper may observe?

definitions.text: Beelzebub's presence unfortunate camper may observe?

parts.words: Beelzebub's presence unfortunate camper may observe?
parts.note: a camper unlucky enough to find the devil sharing their canvas shelter would see wickedness inside it, and the same letters make a phrase for malicious purpose

explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as EVIL IN TENT: the devil's wickedness inside a camper's tent. Run together, the words mean a wicked purpose.
explanation.definitionFit: A malicious purpose or design, the wicked aim behind an act.

clue.text: Some clever Dick or musical Giuseppe?

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Is this a smart alec or a famous Italian composer?
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition included 'or', but 'or' only links the wordplay to 'musical Giuseppe'.
explanation.definitionFit: Giuseppe Verdi was the Italian opera composer of Aida and La Traviata.

clue.text: Gobbler wants skinless meat served in long pot

parts.note: an epic is a long tale, so epic suggests great length

indicators.note: served in places the trimmed meat inside the pot

parts.note: an urn is a pot or vase

indicators.note: skinless means the outer letters of meat are peeled away

explanation.surface: A greedy eater wants meat with the skin off, served in a tall pot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'long' as EPIC means lengthy, as in an epic film.
explanation.definitionFit: A lover of fine food; the clue's word for a glutton stretches the sense, since a gourmet is about pleasure in eating.
